A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same training-free diffusion compression framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F are available and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original Gaussian simulations and compression experiments on CIFAR-10, Kodak, and DIV2K, including quantitative metrics, latency measurements, and reconstruction examples in Section V and Appendix F.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds compression-baseline results in Figures 5, 11, and 12 and latency comparisons in Table I.

M1.justification: The RCC/PFR framework and discrete decoder in Eq. (7) remain unchanged. V2 locally corrects the written procedure: Eq. (6) uses the current-time score, and Algorithm 1 conditions its selection ratio on z_{k+1} instead of a candidate-indexed quantity. These are specification corrections; an implementation change is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions cover scalar Gaussian simulations and image compression on CIFAR-10, Kodak, and DIV2K. No additional dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: Figures 5 and 11 add evaluated DLF, StableCodec, RDEIC, and OneDC comparisons to the existing HiFiC, CDC, BPG, and DDCM comparisons. Table I additionally compares OneDC and StableCodec latency and model size. This substantially broadens the evaluated competing methods; CIFAR-10 comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated datasets, sample counts, metrics, diffusion backbones, parameter sweeps, and DDCM configurations are retained. V2 newly documents DDIM steps, guidance, coding candidates, and bitstream measurement, but does not establish that these settings replaced different settings in v1.

E4.justification: The existing t/rho sensitivity analyses, diffusion-backbone comparisons, and reconstruction case studies are retained. The added baseline curves extend benchmark comparisons; the new discussion supplies explanations and limitations without adding ablation or robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars. The FID estimation description and shared-randomness mechanism do not introduce a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial comparative results in Figures 5, 11, and 12. Table I newly reports total latency of 0.74 seconds for both OneDC and StableCodec. DDCM bitrate labels also change in Figures 5 and 11, including 0.020 to 0.022 BPP. The proposed method's Table III MSE/FID values and reconstruction examples remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The existing Gaussian theory receives mathematical repairs and qualifications. V2 corrects Theorem 4's reversed one-shot rate bound, adds the valid perception range to Proposition 2, and explicitly qualifies Lemma 1 and Appendix C expressions by T approaching infinity. Appendices B–E correct noise scaling, variance and DP expressions; Appendix C additionally identifies the rho=1 optimal-transport solution. The theorem structure and principal optimality conclusions are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction now explicitly qualifies multivariate Gaussian DP optimality with per-dimension scaling, making the contribution summary consistent with the condition already present in v1's Theorem 3. The abstract, conclusion, and central claims of training-free RDP traversal and scalar Gaussian RDP optimality are otherwise retained.

C2.justification: New Section VI substantially expands the earlier scattered qualifications. It discusses computational obstacles to dimension-specific water-filling, proposes a Gaussian-latent explanation while acknowledging missing latent-space theory, and interprets the latency-versus-flexibility tradeoff against one-step methods. Appendix F also recommends model- and dataset-specific rho calibration.

D1.justification: Appendix F-B1 adds concrete implementation disclosures: a 50-step DDIM scheduler, bitrate-dependent denoising steps, no guidance, 12–16-bit PFR chunks, candidate-pool sizes, chunk timings, and actual-bitstream rate measurement. It also adds calibration guidance. These clarify existing experiments; the hardware and previously provided access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds recent compression references, including DLF, RDEIC, OneDC, and StableCodec, plus DDIM. It extends the positioning against methods requiring trained adapters or distillation and discusses their deployment tradeoffs. The foundational DP/RDP positioning remains intact; PSC's publication update refers to the same existing work.

P1.justification: V2 inserts a Discussions section before the conclusion, expands the implementation subsection, revises baseline descriptions, adds funding acknowledgments, and makes localized language and terminology corrections. Most existing prose and the overall main-text/appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figures 5, 11, and 12 are redrawn with expanded comparator legends, revised colors, and inline bitrate annotations. Figures 5 and 11 display fewer existing timestep curves. Table I gains rows and moves above Figure 6, with other figures reflowing between pages. The remaining graphics and reconstruction images are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves mathematical consistency through the corrected rate bound and qualified derivations, strengthens comparison with contemporary codecs, and makes implementation choices more reproducible. The expanded discussion better exposes applicability and deployment limits. These provide clear, bounded improvements to the existing contribution; latent-space optimality remains unresolved, and the expanded plot legends modestly reduce readability.
